papers_read.title_as_printed: Comparing a pre-defined versus deep learning approach for extracting brain atrophy patterns to predict cognitive decline due to Alzheimer's disease in patients with mild cognitive symptoms (Arvidsson et al., Alzheimer's Research & Therapy 2024)
Benchmarking parametric models of disease progression for early detection of cognitive decline (Platero & Bengoa, Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine 2026)

what_each_reports.P-274: Four-year progression from SCD/MCI to AD dementia (CSF-confirmed) in 332 BioFINDER-1 patients, double cross-validation: clinical-data model AUC 0.850, clinical + hippocampal volume AUC 0.862 (CI 0.728-0.960), FreeSurfer model 0.832, DL model 0.840; external ADNI MCI subset (n=108): FreeSurfer 0.688, DL 0.799, others not significantly different from BioFINDER test.
what_each_reports.P-33: Per-visit AUC of a Bayesian-KDE classifier assigning clinical status (CU vs MCI) from the disease progression score of parametric DPMs trained on neuropsychological scores only, ADNI (536 sCU, 114 pCU, 513 sMCI), 20% test split: Leaspy AUC 0.96 (0.006), RPDPM 0.94, GRACE 0.92-0.93.

quantity_a: AUC for predicting conversion from SCD/MCI to AD dementia within four years; memory-clinic SCD+MCI population (BioFINDER-1); predictors = demographics, MMSE, ADAS delayed recall, APOE plus hippocampal volume (structural MRI).
quantity_b: AUC for classifying the current clinical status (cognitively unimpaired vs MCI) at each visit from a latent disease-progression score fitted to longitudinal neuropsychological scores; ADNI CU and stable-MCI participants (MCI converters to dementia excluded).
incompatible_if_same: Only in a weak sense: 0.862 (CI 0.728-0.960) vs 0.96 (SD 0.006 across bootstraps); the P-274 interval nearly reaches 0.96, and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes. The question does not arise because the estimands differ.

gates.task: mismatch: P-274 is prognostic MCI/SCD-to-AD-dementia conversion; P-33's AUC is diagnostic CU-vs-MCI status classification per visit (its prognostic analysis concerns CU-to-MCI conversion, not MCI-to-dementia).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: P-274 develops and tests on BioFINDER-1 (ADNI only as a 108-patient external check); P-33 is ADNI-1/2/3 only.
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-274 internal double CV plus external ADNI evaluation; P-33 internal bootstrap train/test split within ADNI.
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-274 best model uses clinical data plus structural MRI hippocampal volume; P-33 uses neuropsychological tests only.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both are ROC-AUC, but for different endpoints (future AD dementia within 4 years vs present CU/MCI status) and different populations.
performance_validity: not a performance comparison in the excluded sense; flag not tripped by either value (0.862, 0.96 with n=1163 and a held-out test split).
independence: Distinct studies and authors; P-274's external ADNI subset could overlap ADNI participants in P-33, but P-274's headline estimate is from BioFINDER.
grounds: P-274's AUC is for four-year progression from SCD/MCI to AD dementia in BioFINDER, whereas P-33's AUC is for classifying CU vs MCI status at each visit in ADNI, so the endpoints differ.
P-33 explicitly excluded MCI participants who progressed to dementia, so its population contains no instance of P-274's outcome.
The predictor sets differ (clinical + hippocampal MRI volume vs neuropsychological scores only) and the dataset families differ (BioFINDER vs ADNI), with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: The primary binary outcome was four-year progression to AD dementia, where a clinical diagnosis of AD dementia during the four years follow-up was considered as a progression.
Adding intracranial and hippocampal volume to the clinical data model increased the test AUC to 0.862 (CI 0.728-0.960)
MCI participants whose last visit indicated either reversion to CU or progression to dementia were excluded from the analysis to specifically characterize the transition from normal cognition to MCI.
Area Under the Curve (AUC) of the Bayesian-KDE classifier at each visit, based on clinical diagnoses.
The results show that Leaspy achieved the highest overall performance, with a top AUC of 0.96

record_defects: dataset_equal 'Yes' is wrong: P-274's development and test cohort is BioFINDER-1, not ADNI (ADNI is a 108-patient external check); the index registry row also lists P-274 Dataset as ADNI.

modality_family 'clinical_survey' with modality_family_equal 'Yes' contradicts the record's own resolution_note ('Modality mismatch: P-274=structural_MRI vs P-33=clinical_survey'); P-274's best model uses structural MRI hippocampal volume.
Both claims labelled 'T2', but P-33's AUC 0.96 is a diagnostic CU-vs-MCI status AUC, not an MCI-progression AUC.

resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' rests on a list of ~45 'bridging' papers that report assorted metrics with no stated separating condition; this is not bridging evidence under the rule.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only a P-33 result for MCI-to-AD-dementia conversion (it reports none) or a P-274 result for CU-vs-MCI classification would put the two on one estimand.
